title: Spacetime Physics: Introduction to Special Relativity (Second Edition)
institution: W. H. Freeman and Company (1992); released by the authors on eftaylor.com
description: Classic introduction to special relativity built around the invariant spacetime interval: Chapter 1 Spacetime: Overview; 2 Floating Free; 3 Same Laws for All; Special Topic: Lorentz Transformation; 4 Trip to Canopus; 5 Trekking through Spacetime; 6 Regions of Spacetime; 7 Momenergy; 8 Collide. Create. Annihilate.; 9 Gravity: Curved Spacetime in Action; answers to odd-numbered exercises; index. Time is measured in metres and c is a conversion factor.
rightsNotes: The authors' download page (eftaylor.com/spacetimephysics/) states under the heading 'FREE TO DOWNLOAD, PRINT, AND SHARE': 'The entire contents of this book are now available under a Creative Commons license. Feel free to download, print, share, translate, and adapt, as long as you follow the (minimal) requirements of the license.' and 'This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.' (seen 2026-10-30).

The scanned copyright page inside the PDFs still carries the 1992 W. H. Freeman notice; the authors' CC BY 4.0 release on their page governs the files offered there. Attribution to Taylor and Wheeler is required and is given on every locator.

Convention: the book writes (interval)² = (time separation)² − (space separation)² for timelike pairs and reverses the order for spacelike pairs so that the interval is always a non-negative real number (Section 1.4). This is the opposite overall sign to Corniversity's (−,+,+,+) line element; units are chosen so that time is measured in metres (c = 1).

versions.label: Second edition (W. H. Freeman, 1992), authors' CC BY 4.0 scans on eftaylor.com
versions.verifiedBy: Corniversity Codex authors and independent physics reviewer; actual chapter PDF text inspected, with selected page-image checks for notation. Review scopes and source hashes are recorded in PHY-210/REVIEW.md and source-review-manifest.json.
componentsSeen: download page: heading 'Spacetime Physics, Second Edition', CC BY 4.0 statement, list of fourteen PDFs (full book via Internet Archive, cover and contents, nine chapters, Special Topic, index, answers to odd-numbered exercises)
00_cover_toc.pdf (12 pages): title page, copyright page (© 1992 Taylor and Wheeler, eleventh printing), contents with section titles and printed page numbers for all chapters
01_chapter1.pdf (24 pages, printed pages 1–24): Sections 1.1–1.5, Sample Problems 1-1 and 1-2, exercises
03_chapter3.pdf (42 pages, printed pages 53–94): Sections 3.1–3.9 and Chapter 3 exercises
04a_special_topic.pdf (26 pages, printed pages 95–120): Sections L.1–L.8 and Special Topic exercises

2026-11-12: actual chapter PDFs 2 and 4–9, including free-float frame limits, worldlines/proper time, causal regions, four-momentum, collisions and local gravity; original problem calculations independently recomputed. This records text inspection, not a claim that every scanned page was visually inspected.
limitations: The PDFs are page scans with an OCR text layer (image coverage 1.00 on every page); the OCR contains errors, so quotations must be checked against the page image.

The PDFs carry no PDF page labels. Printed page numbers were read from the running heads and the contents page; printedPageLabel values below are those printed numbers (physical index 0 of Chapter 1 is printed page 1; of Chapter 3, page 53; of the Special Topic, page 95).
The answers file covers odd-numbered exercises only.
The index and odd-numbered answers file were listed but are not needed for the original problem sheets and are not claimed as reviewed here.

The 1992 text uses neutrinos as massless/light-speed examples (including chapter 5 p.153 and chapter 6 p.176). Neutrino oscillations establish nonzero mass differences; the course uses photons as its physical null-particle example.
